subject: Order form: audit rights / pen-test scope boundaries
messages:
From: David Li <david.li@acmehealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — audit rights & pen-test scope questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the draft order form. Before we finalize, Security has a couple of asks we need clarified in the MSA/Order Form:

1) Audit scope: we need SOC 2 reports and an ability to request "reasonable" evidence (logs, config exports) on a quarterly cadence for the systems that process PHI.
2) Pen test language: we prefer a defined test window and limited blast radius — i.e., no social engineering, no physical testing, and a maximum of 48 hours of active exploitation.
3) Inspection rights: we want a path to an on-site inspection for high-risk integrations, but this would be narrow and scheduled in advance.
4) Evidence cadence: can you propose a pragmatic cadence for providing SOC2 evidence and any pen-test corroboration? Weekly deliveries are unrealistic for us to consume.

I'm attaching a short document with Acme's expectations (acme-audit-ask-2026.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's position and what language you can commit to in the Order Form?

Thanks,
David Li
Director, Security Engineering
Acme Health

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Li <david.li@acmehealth.com>, security-team@acmehealth.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — audit rights & pen-test scope questions

Hi David — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Looping in Ben (AE) and Laura (Legal).

High-level proposal from Redwood:
- SOC 2: we will provide annual SOC 2 Type II report plus a quarterly evidence package for in-scope controls limited to the environment used by Acme. Evidence package will include configuration snapshots, relevant exception tickets, and access logs for the affected tenant(s).
- Pen-test: we agree to a bounded testing window and exclusions for social engineering and physical testing. We propose a maximum active testing window of 72 hours and require a pre-test scope and test plan sign-off. We can accept a 48-hour cap if Acme prefers; Laura, please confirm the legal implications.
- Inspection rights: Redwood prefers documentary and remote evidence first; on-site inspections should be available by exception with 30 days' notice and an agreed scope. We will not permit unlimited ad-hoc on-site access.
- Evidence cadence: suggest monthly evidence bundles for operational artifacts and ad-hoc for incident-related items. Quarterly is acceptable if Acme wants lower frequency.

Next steps: Laura to draft redline language for the MSA and Order Form (audit rights + pen-test appendix). Ben — can you confirm commercial impact for adding a limited inspection clause?

Attaching a quick redline skeleton I've been using (redline_MSA_tessa_v1.docx) for context.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, David Li <david.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — audit rights & pen-test scope questions

Thanks — quick commercial note: adding broad on-site inspection rights typically triggers a pricing/commitment uplift for Dedicated customers. For Hosted customers we handle documentary/remote evidence under standard terms. If Acme needs on-site inspection as a standard right vs. a scheduled exception, we should surface that as an order-form add-on (one-time fee + travel).

I'll flag this in the deal record (ACME-2026-Q2-4521) and can propose a structured add-on in the quote. For now let's propose the exception-based on-site path (30-day notice) and keep the default to remote evidence.

Ben
Senior Enterprise AE
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, David Li <david.li@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — audit rights & pen-test scope questions

David / team — copying Redwood's proposed redline text below for quick review. This is intended to be prescriptive and limited to reduce ambiguity.

Proposed clause (MSA, Security Exhibit):
"Customer may request access to Redwood Inference's SOC 2 Type II report and supporting documentary evidence for in-scope systems. Documentary evidence includes configuration exports, console logs, and written attestations related to the controls in scope. Documentary requests shall be limited to a reasonable scope and will be delivered as monthly or quarterly bundles as agreed in the Order Form.

On-site inspections are available only by exception, require at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, and are limited to the systems processing Customer Data as specified in the Order Form. On-site inspections shall be subject to agreed scope, timing, and security procedures; Redwood may require a mutually agreed Statement of Work (including travel and administrative fees) for on-site inspections.

Penetration testing: Customer-initiated penetration tests are permitted if (a) pre-approved test plan and scope are provided at least fourteen (14) days in advance; (b) social engineering and physical intrusion are expressly excluded; and (c) active exploitation time is limited to seventy-two (72) hours unless otherwise agreed in writing. Redwood will coordinate a post-test evidence handoff and a remediation discussion."

I've attached a redlined MSA for internal review (redline_MSA_tessa_v1.docx). If Acme accepts, we can integrate this language into the Order Form.

—Laura
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: David Li <david.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — audit rights & pen-test scope questions

Laura / Tessa — thank you for the thorough response and the draft language. A few quick points from Acme:
- Monthly bundles are preferred for operational evidence; quarterly is acceptable for higher-level attestations.
- We can accept the 72-hour active window for pen-tests if Redwood provides the post-test remediation summary and logs for any findings.
- On-site by exception + 30-day notice is workable; we'd like a maximum of two on-site days per inspection and a capped list of systems to be inspected.

I'll take the proposed clause back to Procurement for a final read; I attached our short pen-test checklist (acme-pen-test-checklist.xlsx) for Laura's reference. If Procurement agrees, we can move forward with the redline and sign the Order Form pending the SOW for on-site delivery costs if needed.

Thanks — David
Director, Security Engineering
Acme Health
